newsitem.title: GERMANY: BoS's Rojo - rate cut due to lower inflation outlook.
newsitem.headline: BoS's Rojo - rate cut due to lower inflation outlook.

text.p: Spanish central bank governor Luis Angel Rojo said on Tuesday that a cut earlier in the day in Spain's key money market rate by the Bank of Spain was due to a downward revision of the country's inflation outlook.
"We had to revise downwards our expectation for the evolution of general inflation and so the reduction of interest rates today was normal," said Rojo.

Asked whether there was room for a further rate easing in the near term, Rojo said: "This will depend on the evolution of the inflation rate on the one hand and of course on deficits and the markets, which are very important."

Rojo was speaking after a meeting of the European Monetary Institute (EMI) council in Frankfurt. The Bank of Spain cut its key money rate to 5.50 percent from 5.75 percent at today's regular repurchase tender for central bank certificates.
